items.title: Source-preserving fixes and suggestions, the closure property, and the four broken autofixes
items.fromShadcn: shadcn never --fixes a guess: its rules are hasSuggestions, not fixable (lint/src/rules/no-unknown-classes.ts:37-41, 128-137). Each suggestion rewrites only inside the literal's own raw text, keeps quotes and entities, replaces one whole class, and offers nothing rather than a wrong edit (lint/src/rules/fixes.ts:1-4, 11-23, 25-47, 66-83; lint/src/grammar/classes.ts:106-127, where withBase keeps variants and '!'). Its hostile-source suite: lint/test/suggestion-safety.test.ts:25-102 (entities and real newlines survive, entity-joined classes get none, JS keeps its quotes, a line continuation disables). Ledger adds two things shadcn lacks: a closure property (a replacement may not fail another Ledger rule), and real T1 autofixes.
items.ledgerToday: Partial. There are two fixable rules. no-deprecated-token calls fixer.replaceText(node, JSON.stringify(node.value.replace(base, dep.replacementClass))) (ds/eslint-plugin/index.js:818-825): a substring replace followed by re-serialisation. Its message drops the variant (:817). no-deprecated-name writes the canonical name over the whole tag (index.js:900) and renames props with no collision check (:901-903), although the attribute path does check (:860-864). rule() already accepts extra meta (index.js:353-356), and withAllowance spreads whole descriptors, so `suggest` survives it (ds/eslint-plugin/gate-rules.js:82-120). The only fix test is ds/test/lint-gates.test.mjs:386-437 (one-to-one renames, no hostile input); no-deprecated-token has no test at all.
items.design:
1. New ds/eslint-plugin/fixes.js, a port of lint/src/rules/fixes.ts:25-47 and lint/src/grammar/classes.ts:117-127.
- replaceClassInSource(node, sourceCode, token, replacement) works on Literal nodes only; TemplateElement quasis and Identifier keys get none, as today (index.js:63-65).
- It takes raw = sourceCode.getText(node) and keeps the quote character.
- A JS string must satisfy raw inner === node.value, so there are no escapes and no line continuation.
- A JSX attribute string is refused when raw contains '&' (an entity). JSX strings have no backslash escapes.
- It splits the inner text on /(\s+)/ and replaces only a token exactly equal to `token`, so hover:fill-chart-categorical-8 is matched whole and keeps its variants. Separators are kept byte for byte, so a real newline stays a newline.
- It returns null when nothing matched verbatim.
- suggestionsFor(node, context, token, replacements[]) returns [{desc, fix}], or undefined, never [].
- withVariants(parsed, base) rebuilds 'variants:…:!base'.
2. Tiers.
- T1 `fix` (--fix) is only for a declared or byte-identical replacement: a deprecated token's replacementClass from utilities.json, or a canonical spelling verified byte-identical at build time (prefer-canonical-class).
- T2 is one suggestion: an exact value equivalent or a unique spelling.
- T3 is several labelled suggestions: nearest steps and ties.
- T4 is none.
3. Closure. Export the class predicates from index.js: isKnown, isMargin, isAlphaToken, isDarkVariant, staticDesignValue, deprecatedClass, and later variantKnown and ownerOf. offerReplacement(cls) is false unless every predicate passes on the rebuilt class.
4. no-deprecated-token (index.js:809-829).
- The message is built from withVariants, so the variant survives.
- The fix goes through replaceClassInSource.
- When that returns null, the message appends that no automatic fix is offered.
5. no-deprecated-name (index.js:896-907).
- Rewrite only the member tail after the local root: localPrefix = jsxTag(node.name) minus the canonical deprecated suffix, then write localPrefix plus the tail of dep.to.
- Skip a prop rename when jsxAttr(node, target) already exists, as :860-864 does, and keep reporting the old prop.
6. ds/test/lint-fix-safety.test.mjs. For every rule with meta.fixable or hasSuggestions, run Linter.verifyAndFix and splice each suggestion over a hostile-source table. Assert:
- (a) ts.createSourceFile(output, TSX) has no parseDiagnostics;
- (b) the rule no longer reports;
- (c) configs.recommended reports nothing new;
- (d) every JSX root identifier in the output is bound by an import or a declaration;
- (e) no element has duplicate attributes;
- (f) the tokens that were not replaced are byte-identical (classesOf before and after).
A property test runs every emitted replacement over the probe battery through all class predicates.

fit-noise.problems:
No conflict with the product contract, and no noise, because reports are unchanged.

Two details are missing:
1. classesOf strips a leading or trailing `!` into the same base (index.js:177). withVariants has to record which position it came from, or a `hover:!bg-x` fix becomes `hover:bg-x!`.
2. The closure predicate list has to grow with the ownership map (one-owner-per-class) and with variantKnown (no-unknown-variant). A replacement must also not move the class to a different owner.
fit-noise.revision:
Keep as designed, with two additions:
- withVariants keeps the `!` position.
- The closure check calls classify(rebuilt).owner === null, in addition to the per-rule predicates.

feasibility.evidence: Read packages/design-system/eslint-plugin/index.js:809-829. The no-deprecated-token fix at :818-825 is JSON.stringify(node.value.replace(base, …)). no-deprecated-name writes dep.to over the whole tag at :900 and renames props at :901-903 with no collision check. The attribute path does check, at :860-864. utilities.json 'deprecated' has exactly one entry: color.chart.categorical.8 → fill-chart-categorical-7. withAllowance spreads the descriptor (gate-rules.js:104-109), so fix and suggest survive it. grep finds no test file in ds/test or scripts/tests that names no-deprecated-token. All four fix:true entries in deprecatedNames (index.js:413-436: Shell.Brand, Shell.NavGroup, Shell.NavItem, Shell.User) keep the root 'Shell'. api/public-api.json exports only '.' and './cn', so named exports from eslint-plugin/index.js need no ds:api:update. shadcn: lint/src/rules/fixes.ts:25-47, lint/src/grammar/classes.ts:117-127.
feasibility.problems:
1. Effort is understated. The closure predicates (isMargin, isAlphaToken, isDarkVariant, staticDesignValue, deprecatedClass) do not exist as functions: they are inline regexes inside each rule (index.js:733-806) and must be extracted first. The item also needs a harness that checks TS parse, bindings and duplicate attributes.
2. The alias spec, 'jsxTag minus the canonical deprecated suffix', is ambiguous. For <DsShell.NavItem> the canonical name is Shell.NavItem, and no textual suffix of the tag equals it.
3. Nothing stops a future fix:true entry whose target root differs from its source root; for such an entry the prefix-preserving rewrite is wrong.
feasibility.revision:
Effort M, batch 1.
1. Rewrite the tag as: the local segments before the canonical root (the alias 'DsShell', or 'Kit.Shell' for a namespace), plus dep.to without its first segment.
2. Report with no fix when dep.to's root differs from the deprecated name's root.
3. Extract the class predicates into eslint-plugin/classes.js in this change, so one-owner-per-class reuses them rather than moving them again.
4. Keep the hostile-source table as designed.

items.title: Settings and options are validated or warned about once, never silently ignored
items.fromShadcn: shadcn has a warnOnce channel whose comment reads 'Silence is the worst failure mode for an enforcement tool', with an injectable sink for tests (lint/src/project/warn.ts:1-20). A string-or-array setting goes through strings(), which warns once on a wrong type (lint/src/rules/settings.ts:14-24). Near-miss config entries are errors with 'Did you mean' (lint/src/rules/contracts.ts:220-251). Tests: lint/test/settings.test.ts:99-107, 170-247.
items.ledgerToday:
Partial.
- settings.ledger.classFunctions is spread with no type check (ds/eslint-plugin/index.js:25-26), so a string is spread into characters.
- A missing utilities.json throws (index.js:13-14). This is good.
- The allow schema rejects unknown keys (gate-rules.js:69-75). This is good.
- An allowance is checked only when its file is linted (gate-rules.js:89-92), so an entry for a deleted file is never noticed.
- withAllowance returns a rule that has its own schema unchanged (gate-rules.js:83-84), so that rule silently gets no allowance support.
items.design:
1. New ds/eslint-plugin/warn.js. warnOnce(key, message) writes '[ledger] …' to stderr once per key per process. setWarningSink(fn) replaces the sink in tests.
2. settings(context) replaces the inline read at index.js:25-26.
- classFunctions, and later variantFunctions, note and kit, accept a string (normalised to [string]) or an array of strings.
- Anything else warns once and falls back to the built-ins.
- An unknown key under settings.ledger warns with a did-you-mean against the known keys.
3. withAllowance (gate-rules.js:82-120) merges a rule's own schema properties into allowSchema instead of returning early at :83-84. note-option then adds `note` in the same place.
4. Dead entries. On the first create per rule and cwd, fs.existsSync each allow key relative to context.cwd and warnOnce for a missing file. scripts/check-allow-lists.mjs already walks every leaf (:36-43); it also fails when a key of scripts/lint-allow.json or ds/test/lint-allow.json names a file that does not exist.

feasibility.evidence:
index.js:25-26 spreads settings.ledger.classFunctions with no type check, so a string becomes characters. gate-rules.js:83-84 returns early for a rule with its own schema; every rule today has schema [] (index.js:353-356, gate-rules.js:122-125, composition-rules.js:30-33), so this is latent. Dead allowance entries are already caught by the package tests:
- packages/design-system/test/lint-gates.test.mjs:264-273: the kit's lint-allow.json files must exist.
- :451-463: scripts/lint-allow.json files must exist.
- :465-476: eslint-suppressions.json files must exist, and no ledger rule may appear there.
The withAllowance proxy replaces options with [] (gate-rules.js:94-97).
feasibility.problems:
1. Point 4 (dead entries) duplicates the three existing tests. The claim 'an entry for a deleted file is never noticed' is false for this repo; a lint-time warning would only help third-party consumers.
2. Merging a rule's schema into allowSchema is not enough. In any file with an allowance, the proxy at gate-rules.js:96 passes options: [], so a merged option (note) never reaches the rule.
feasibility.revision:
Effort S.
1. Keep warn.js, settings() and the schema merge.
2. In the proxy, pass options: [{ ...context.options[0], allow: undefined }] instead of [].
3. Drop the check-allow-lists change. Keep at most a consumer-side warnOnce for a missing file.

items.title: Close the escape routes: counted and reasoned disables, unused directives as errors, the examples directory, and the lint scope
items.fromShadcn: shadcn's evals classify any eslint-disable, <style> or inline style in a changed file as a workaround, after the fact (packages/evals/lib/classify.mjs:97-106; run.mjs:55-61). Its red team found 2 escapes outside JSX (docs/evals.md:185-186). Its adoption guide asks for a reason on every disable, through eslint-comments require-description (docs/adoption.md:149-160). Ledger turns that detection into CI gates. It keeps its closed option model: no allow, deny, contracts or message options as in lint/src/rules/policy-schema.ts:1-36, only per-file counts that shrink.
items.ledgerToday:
Better on options, partial on bypasses. Per-file two-way allowances (gate-rules.js:67-120) and growth refusal against the base ref (scripts/check-allow-lists.mjs:22-84) are stricter than anything shadcn has. The bypasses:
- 5 inline disables of ledger rules in the kit are counted nowhere. Two give no reason: ds/src/components/card.tsx:122 and empty.tsx:71 (both no-arbitrary-value). Three give one: alert.tsx:32, avatar.tsx:232, patterns/chart/_marks.tsx:100.
- _marks.tsx:100 disables no-non-token-class for a class index.js:338 already admits, so ESLint warns 'Unused eslint-disable directive'.
- Neither eslint.config.js nor ds/eslint.config.js sets linterOptions.reportUnusedDisableDirectives.
- src/components/examples is lint-ignored (eslint.config.js:88-90) but missing from REFERENCE_KITS (:18-33), so a screen can import unlinted styled code.
- A new directory under src/ outside PRODUCT (:52-58) would silently lose every ledger rule.
items.design:
1. Add '@/components/examples' and '@/components/examples/*' to REFERENCE_KITS (eslint.config.js:24-30).
2. Set linterOptions.reportUnusedDisableDirectives to 'error' in the root config (after the ignores block at :92) and in ds/eslint.config.js. In the same change, delete the directive at _marks.tsx:100 and any other directive that `eslint . --report-unused-disable-directives-severity error` lists.
3. Disables join the ratchet as a computed list, not a committed block. A 'disables' block added to an existing lint-allow.json would itself fail check-allow-lists as 'new' (:61-64).
- scripts/check-allow-lists.mjs runs a git grep for ledger disables at the base ref and in the working tree, over src and packages/design-system/src.
- It builds {'<file> › <rule>': count} and reuses the growth comparison at :60-69.
4. New rule ledger/disable-reason, in both presets. It reads sourceCode.getAllComments() and reports an eslint-disable of a ledger/* rule that has no ' -- ' reason. Add reasons to card.tsx:122 and empty.tsx:71 in the same change. The alternative is @eslint-community/eslint-comments/require-description, which is one more dependency.
5. scripts/tests/design-system-boundary.test.mjs (run by test:app) gains 'no product file disables a ledger rule inline'. There are 0 such files today.
6. A scope test in the same file walks src/**/*.{ts,tsx}.
- await eslint.isPathIgnored(f) must equal membership in an explicit IGNORED list: examples, reui, ui and the generated nist and cci files.
- Otherwise the rule ledger/no-non-token-class resolves to error for f, unless f is in NOT_UI: src/routeTree.gen.ts, src/server.ts and the third file scope.mjs found.
7. Options stay closed: allow, plus note from note-option.
items.liveEvidence:
scratch/harvest-infra/escape-dirs.mjs, run through the root config with lintText:
- A Pill component with className="bg-pink-500 rounded-full px-6 text-[13px]" in src/components/prototype gives no-arbitrary-value plus 2 no-non-token-class.
- The same file in src/components/examples, reui or ui is ignored.
- import { Pill } from '@/components/examples/pill' in src/routes/vendors.tsx is allowed, while the reui and ui paths are blocked.
scope.mjs: of 186 src files, only src/routeTree.gen.ts, src/server.ts and one other get no ledger rules.
grep, verified in this session: 5 ledger disables in the kit, 0 in product, 2 without a reason.
items.messageDraft:
disable-reason: 'This eslint-disable of ledger/no-arbitrary-value gives no reason. Add "-- <why this site needs it>"; disables are counted with the allowances and only shrink.'
examples import: 'src/components/examples is a look-only reference sample, not product code, and the lint does not read it. Import the kit from @ledger/design-system or move the component under src/components/app.'
check-allow-lists: 'src/components/prototype/foo.tsx › ledger/no-margin is new: an inline eslint-disable of a ledger rule. Fix the site instead.'
items.noiseRisk: Low. The 4 used kit disables are the starting counts. The unused directive must be deleted before 'error' lands. Two kit sites need a reason.
items.openQuestion: check-allow-lists cannot tell a rule landing from growth: a new ledger/<rule> key in an existing lint-allow.json fails as 'new' (scripts/check-allow-lists.mjs:61-64). So today every new or strengthened rule must land at zero findings, or fix its sites in the same batch. Should a key for a rule that did not exist at the base ref (checked against the plugin's rule names at the base ref) count as that rule's gate landing? Or should new rules keep landing at zero?
testCases: src/routes/vendors.tsx importing '@/components/examples/pill' gives no-restricted-imports (allowed today)
a sixth `eslint-disable-next-line ledger/no-arbitrary-value` in ds/src/components/badge.tsx makes check:allow-lists fail with '… › ledger/no-arbitrary-value is new'
`// eslint-disable-next-line ledger/no-margin` with no reason gives ledger/disable-reason; `// eslint-disable-next-line ledger/no-margin -- Overlap is the geometry` gives none
the unused directive at _marks.tsx:100 fails `npm run lint -w packages/design-system` until it is deleted (a warning today)
a product file with `// eslint-disable-next-line ledger/no-margin` fails design-system-boundary.test.mjs
scope: a new src/features/billing.tsx with className='bg-red-500' must resolve ledger/no-non-token-class to error or be listed in the scope test
removing a disable passes (counts only shrink)

fit-noise.problems:
1. The computed list and ledger/disable-reason only see `eslint-disable`. An inline rule-config comment turns ledger rules off, or down to warn, with no disable keyword. The boundary test "no product file disables a ledger rule inline" would pass it.
2. A root eslint-suppressions.json is an unguarded bypass: ESLint applies it on `npm run lint`, and no list checks it.
3. Asking for a reason at card.tsx:122 and empty.tsx:71 treats a policy gap as a site exception. Ledger's own definition of structure is "no colour, size, space" (index.js:247), and those templates have none.
4. disable-reason's draft message contains 'eslint-disable' and 'allowances'. meta-and-message-tests' banned-phrase regex (/eslint-disable|allowance|…/) would fail it in batch 2.
5. Stories run no-non-token-class at 'warn' (index.js:1170). A new story with bg-red-500 passes CI.
fit-noise.revision:
Keep items 1, 2, 5 and 6 as designed, and add the following.

(a) The disables ratchet greps both forms: `eslint-disable(-next)?-line? … ledger/` and block config comments `/* eslint … ledger/<rule>: … */`.

(b) Replace disable-reason with ledger/no-inline-config, in both presets. Its messages avoid the banned words. It reports:
- any inline config comment that sets a ledger/* rule, always;
- an eslint-disable of ledger/* without a ' -- ' reason.
Example message: 'This comment turns ledger/no-margin off for the file. Fix the class; a site that must keep it states why after " -- ".'

(c) check-allow-lists fails in either case:
- a root ./eslint-suppressions.json exists;
- any suppressions file (root or ds/eslint-suppressions.json) holds a ledger/* key.
The message: 'eslint-suppressions.json may not carry ledger rules; they ratchet through lint-allow.json.'

(d) Admit length-free arbitrary grid templates as structural, then delete the directives at alert.tsx:32, card.tsx:122 and empty.tsx:71 instead of adding reasons.
- Admitted: `grid-(cols|rows)-[…]` whose `_`-separated tracks are only auto, <n>fr, minmax(0,<n>fr|auto), min-content, max-content or subgrid.
- Still reported: the 4 px-carrying templates, such as grid-cols-[220px_minmax(0,1fr)].
- That leaves avatar.tsx:232, which has a reason, and deletes _marks.tsx:100.

(e) Set stories' no-non-token-class to error (0 story warnings today), or run both lints with --max-warnings 0.

feasibility.evidence:
grep: the kit has 5 disables of ledger rules. card.tsx:122 and empty.tsx:71 give no reason; alert.tsx:32, avatar.tsx:232 and patterns/chart/_marks.tsx:100 give one. Product has 0 (its 4 disables are react-hooks/exhaustive-deps).
I ran `eslint --report-unused-disable-directives-severity error`. The kit fails on exactly one site, _marks.tsx:100. The root passes, with 0 unused directives and 21 react-refresh warnings. So 'error' lands with one deletion.
eslint.config.js:18-33 (REFERENCE_KITS) has no examples entry, while :88-90 ignores the directory.
Scope, through ESLint calculateConfigForFile over the 186 src files (scratch harvest-review-feasibility/scope.mjs): 180 get ledger/no-non-token-class; 3 are ignored (reui, and examples ×2); 3 get none (routeTree.gen.ts, server.ts, start.ts).
check-allow-lists.mjs:61-64 fails on any new key. @eslint-community/eslint-plugin-eslint-comments is not installed.
feasibility.revision:
Effort M.
1. Add to the item: the Lint.mdx row, build:llms and a CHANGELOG entry.
2. A simpler alternative to the computed disables list: move the 4 reasoned kit disables into test/lint-allow.json, so there is one shrink-only ledger ratchet, and have disable-reason report every inline disable of a ledger rule.
3. Answer the openQuestion in this batch: a key for a rule that has no row in the base ref's Lint.mdx (read with git show) is that rule landing, not growth.

items.title: Lint through the packed tarball's @ledger/design-system/eslint export in the consumer smoke
items.fromShadcn: shadcn's install smoke packs the tarball and checks its listing: an ESM build, the worker, a README, and no src, scripts or test. Every later batch that adds plugin data (lint.json, parts.json, eslint-plugin/docs/*.md) adds that file to the listing assertion.

items.title: One message contract: meta.messages, messageIds with data, a shared report helper, and allowances that render ids
items.fromShadcn: shadcn's rules keep a MESSAGES table and report {messageId, data} (lint/src/rules/no-raw-colors.ts:138-166; no-restyle.ts:31-32: 'No message tells the reader to change the config: a diagnostic reaches agents'). One reporter interpolates universal and rule slots and appends settings.shadcn.note (lint/src/rules/messages.ts:7-33, 109-120, 136-181). Its wording states the consequence first ('so no CSS is generated for it', no-unknown-classes.ts:27-33). Messages are capped at 500 characters (policy-schema.ts:6). Not taken: the per-rule message replacement.
items.ledgerToday: Partial. Three rule() factories set meta {type, docs:{description}, schema:[]} and nothing else (index.js:353-356, gate-rules.js:122-125, composition-rules.js:30-33). Every message is an inline template at its report call: 47 sites (index.js 29, gate-rules.js 11, composition-rules.js 7). withAllowance rebuilds each report as {...descriptor, message: `${descriptor.message} (…)`} (gate-rules.js:104-109). A messageId rule would therefore print 'undefined (…)', and ESLint throws when a report carries both message and messageId. The best Ledger texts already follow the contract by habit: gate-rules.js:154-155, 188-189, 464, 473.
items.liveEvidence: Meta dump (scratch/harvest-diag/current-messages.txt): 26 rules; 0 with meta.messages, 0 with docs.url, 0 with hasSuggestions; 2 fixable. RuleTester refuses messageId tests today: 'can not use messageId if rule under test doesn't define meta.messages' (harvest-infra/ruletester.mjs). 15 of 26 rules meet what, why and instead; 0 of 26 carry a docs pointer. The rules agents hit most are the weakest: no-non-token-class, no-arbitrary-value, no-static-design-value, no-style-design-value.
items.messageDraft: report.js header: 'A Ledger finding says what was written, what it is, why that matters here and what to write instead, in at most 300 characters. It never offers the configuration as the fix. meta.docs.url points at the rule's page, which has examples and limits.'
items.noiseRisk: None. This changes structure and ids, not what is reported. The one trap is withAllowance's append, which a test covers for every messageId rule.
testCases: withAllowance over a messageId rule, allow {file:1}, 2 reports: both are reported with text rendered from meta.messages plus ' (2 in this file; its allowance is 1)', with no TypeError and no 'undefined (…)'
no-margin reports messageId 'margin' with data {cls:'mt-200'}
style={{ backgroundColor: 'hsl(0 0% 0%)' }} gives a message containing '(hsl(0 0% 0%))' with balanced parentheses
every rule in plugin.rules has non-empty meta.messages, and its source has no inline `message:` (static grep)

fit-noise.problems: The contract measures the cap after interpolation, including {{note}} and the allowance suffix, so the note alone can push any message over. Rule (1), 'the subject comes first, quoted as written', contradicts keeping the 15 good texts, which name a part or an attribute first.
fit-noise.revision:
- Measure the cap on the template rendered with its data, before {{note}} and the ' (n in this file…)' suffix.
- Accept any of these as the subject: "class", <Tag>, Part.Name, attr="…", style.x, or a call().
- use-primitives names at most two advice kinds per report, with the rest in the page's Limits. It could instead report one message per kind.
- Everything else stays as designed.

feasibility.problems:
1. Because the note travels in data, every RuleTester data assertion and every snapshot fixture must carry note:''.
2. 'The url comes from rule-docs-pages', but rule-docs-pages depends on this item: the dependency is circular.
3. withAllowance, as described, re-reports {node, loc, message} and so drops fix and suggest.
4. A per-rule note read from options is blanked by the proxy (gate-rules.js:96).
feasibility.revision:
Effort M; keep the contract.
1. The case-file loader and the snapshot fixture add data.note = '' whenever a case gives data.
2. withAllowance re-reports the descriptor without messageId and data, keeping fix and suggest: {...rest, message}.
3. defineRule leaves docs.url unset until rule-docs-pages fills it.
4. Fix the proxy options as in settings-validation.

items.title: settings.ledger.note and a per-rule note for the product's own pointer
items.fromShadcn: settings.shadcn.note is appended to every finding (lint/src/rules/messages.ts:67-78, 159-181; lint/test/messages.test.ts:371-482; docs/design-systems.md:122-124). Not taken: the per-rule `message` replacement.
items.ledgerToday: None. The kit cannot name app code. no-native-confirm says 'Use AlertDialog for confirmation…' (ds/eslint-plugin/composition-rules.js:209-213), while the app's answer is useConfirmation (docs/guides/product-patterns.md, Forms and confirmations). The root config can only change severity and allow (eslint.config.js:117-128).
items.design:
1. settings.ledger.note is a string of at most 200 characters, trimmed. It is appended to every ledger finding through the {{note}} slot (message-contract).
2. A per-rule {note} option, also at most 200 characters, joins allow in the merged schema (settings-validation's withAllowance change). It is appended after the global note.
3. A non-string warns once and is ignored.

items.design:
scripts/lint-corpus.mjs takes --check, --update and --rule <id>.
- Clean corpus: the PRODUCT globs, packages/design-system/src/** and its stories. Every ledger rule runs at 'warn', opt-in rules included, and allow options are stripped so allowance sites count.
- Stock corpus: ds/test/fixtures/stock-classes.json. It holds the 398 class strings from shadcn's lint/test/fixtures/registry-corpus.json (MIT, notice kept) plus a hand list of Tailwind palette and scale classes. Each string is linted as <div className={JSON.stringify(s)} /> in one synthetic file.
- Baseline scripts/lint-corpus-baseline.json: { clean: {rule: n}, stock: {rule: n}, stockTokensPassing: 205, doubleReported: 80 }.
--check fails when:
- clean[rule] rises;
- stockTokensPassing rises (a stock class now passes: allowlist creep);
- doubleReported rises;
- a file fails to parse, or no files match.
Per-rule stock counts are informational and not ratcheted. one-owner-per-class deliberately moves reports between rules, so a per-rule 'may only rise' check (the infra miner's version) would fail on a correct change.
The baseline is not added to check-allow-lists' LISTS, where a new rule's key would fail as 'new'. Instead, lint-corpus.mjs compares with the baseline at DS_BASE_REF itself (git show) and treats a rule absent at the base as new.
Wire `npm run lint:corpus -- --check` into the ci.yml check job after the package tests (:51-52).

items.design:
scripts/lint-bench.mjs uses the ESLint API over the PRODUCT globs and packages/design-system/src.
- Configurations: parse-only; configs.package; recommended plus the product rules; each ledger rule alone.
- One warm run, then N=5 measured runs. Report the median ms and ms/file.

- --large 5000 writes a temporary project whose files import 8 parts from '@ledger/design-system' with className sites, and symlinks node_modules.
- --plugin <path> compares a side build.

- (a) the per-Program site cache lands in shared-resolver, paired with one-owner-per-class's independence test;

items.design:
New ds/eslint-plugin/identity.js.
kitPartOf(context, nameNode) returns a canonical dotted name, or ''.
- It keeps kitPart's jsxTag recursion (index.js:358-363): an alias resolves through ImportSpecifier.imported, a namespace root is dropped, and three-level names such as Shell.TopNav.Item work.
- It requires an ImportBinding that is not type-only, checking importKind on the declaration and on the specifier (as composition-rules.js:47-50).
- Product mode: the source must be exactly '@ledger/design-system'.
- Package mode (configs.package sets settings.ledger.kit = 'self'): a relative import that resolves under packages/design-system/src/(components|patterns|layout|primitives) or their index barrels (stories import '../../components'), or a same-file top-level declaration whose root is in components.json.
- The root is checked against components.json. Members of a known root are accepted until parts.json lists compound names; after that, Shell.Nope is rejected.
- Results are memoised per file by name text.
classOwnerOf(context, openingElement) returns {part, via: 'self'|'render', wrapper}.
- When a render attribute holds a JSX element, or a function whose returned element spreads its first parameter, the rendered element's kitPartOf wins and the trigger becomes the wrapper.
- A render function that does not spread its props leaves the classes on the trigger.
What changes:
- kitPart, kitName, importedKitName and kitNames become re-exports of kitPartOf.
- Every raw-tag comparison goes: index.js:641-642, :701, :926, and :942 with its ancestor check at :946-950 (Button and TextLink resolve; a and Link stay tag checks).
- The gate rules' overlay checks (gate-rules.js:134, 372, 436) and text-link-navigation and dialog-footer-order (composition-rules.js:217-262) use it too.
- no-deprecated-name's alias map (index.js:835-889) reads identity.

items.design:
In values.js:
1. patternSteps(binding, pattern), a port of collect.ts:403-432, records the route from the declarator to the binding as index and key steps.
2. visitThrough(node, steps, mode) (proto/class-sites.js:126-156) projects those steps into a literal initializer while it is plain, and follows the rest through each branch. A shape it cannot enter is unreadable, never read whole.
3. A default inside the pattern is read as an authored alternative. A rest element, or a spread ahead of the slot, is unreadable ('rest' or 'spread').
4. visitIdentifier (proto:94-122):
- an ImportBinding is unreadable 'imported';
- a Parameter is 'reassigned' if written, otherwise its AssignmentPattern fallback is visited; a className, class or *ClassName key is the forwarded className, which is opaque and sanctioned; any other prop is 'prop';
- a const, let or var with an init is 'reassigned' if written, otherwise the destructuring route is followed.
5. visitMember (proto:190-201). props.className on a Parameter is opaque. A write revokes forwarding ('reassigned'): className ??= …, props.className = …, Object.assign(props, …). An object default is read.
6. If this item slips, a batch-1-sized stopgap: constInitOf returns undefined when definition.node.id is not an Identifier.

- A variant helper visits its config (class-helpers).

- An Identifier callee that resolves to a same-file FunctionDeclaration, or to a never-written const arrow, visits its returns one hop, with a recursion guard.

- A callee const initialised by cva(...) or tv(...) is resolved.

items.design:
A new rule, ledger/no-raw-colour, in gate-rules.js, registered through withAllowance. Its visitors:
1. A JSXAttribute named fill, stroke, color, stopColor, floodColor or lightingColor, when the element is intrinsic (/^[a-z]/) or imported from 'recharts'.
2. recharts object props (cursor, activeDot, dot, tick, label, labelLine, activeShape, background) and style props (contentStyle, wrapperStyle, labelStyle, itemStyle): walk values.objectsOf and read the fill, stroke and color keys.
3. A top-level const array or object whose string values are all raw colours, reported where it is written.
Leaves come from values.leaves. A leaf is raw when its bare text parses as a colour and is not currentColor, none, transparent, inherit, url(#…) or var(--…). Any call passes (token(), chartColor(), surface()).
New ds/eslint-plugin/colours.js holds parseColor and the 148 CSS named colours, a port of lint/src/grammar/colors.ts:9-317. style-colour-completeness shares it.
It runs in configs.package (stories on) and configs.recommended. Consider adding 'recharts' to the product's no-restricted-imports.

items.design:
New ds/eslint-plugin/suggest.js: pure, lazy, and memoised. Prototypes: harvest-oracle/suggest.mjs, harvest-diag/nearest.mjs, harvest-styles/token-index.mjs.
suggestClass returns {cause, text, replacements, single}. The first match wins, and value comes before spelling:
1. A negative on a prefix that takes none is explained, with no replacement.
2. A space key that looks like Ledger's but is not one (p-210) gets its two neighbours, never one.
3. A stock scale value maps by value:
- spacing n × 0.25rem;
- text-* to font-* by size, preferring regular weight;
- rounded-*, font-weights, duration-N and opacity-N to their tokens;
- shadows by log2 of the dominant layer.
An exact match gives one replacement, labelled 'the same value'. Otherwise the two nearest, with deltas; a step further than max(4px, 25%) away is dropped.
4. A numbered series beyond its range states the live range and never respells it.
5. Spelling: within the property family first, then across all 605 admitted names. Keep every candidate tied at the best distance; there is no alphabetical tie-break.
6. One edit from a stock name goes to step 3.
Colours (see the open question):
- (a) near-identical, OKLab ≤ 0.02 in the matching role in both modes: one replacement;
- (b) otherwise, list the hue family's roles: red → danger, accent-red; green → success, accent-green; blue → information, brand, accent-blue; yellow, amber and orange → warning, accent-orange; the greys → neutral, subtle. At most two tokens, ranked by OKLab, each labelled with its purpose.
- The state follows the variant (hover:, active:, disabled:), dark: ranks by the dark value, and specialised tokens are never offered.
Style hints: an exact length in the property's family names the token; a colour within 0.02 adds 'It matches …'; partial values get none.
Wired into no-non-token-class (stock and typo), no-arbitrary-value, no-static-design-value, no-dark-variant, no-alpha-token (sibling states), no-style-design-value and no-raw-colour.

items.design:
A new rule, ledger/no-restyle, in restyle-rules.js. It has no options, runs in recommended only, and reads contextual class sites through classOwnerOf. Each token is decided in this order, with the verdict cached per part and token:
1. Prop-owned: an appearance group is reported. A layout group is reported only when the prop is single-purpose, the class has no responsive or container variant, and it is not a visibility class.
2. A focus target passes.
3. A class the part @accepts passes.
4. An appearance group the part's root sets is reported.
5. Kind defaults:
- a component owns spacing and shape;
- a layout-primitive owns spacing, typography, and fill and text colour;
- a type-primitive owns only what its props emit.
Layout and motion stay the caller's.
6. An unclassified class is skipped.
On the primitives, what use-primitives reports is skipped.
